brief: A bracket to hang my 40-inch TV on the living room wall.

requirements.evidence: 4-cell plate (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,1,0;full) with 4x hex-acc-cleat on rear outer faces; check_build ok, meshClash clear
requirements.requirement: Bracket hangs on the living room wall

requirements.evidence: Catalog has no VESA/TV mount part and no TV prop; configurator checks fit only and 3D-printed material/load rating is unknown — cannot verify holding a 40-inch TV

finish.summary: Built a 4-cell wall plate hung on four French cleats. It provides a wall-mountable bracket body, but there is no VESA/TV attachment in the system and load/strength cannot be verified, so hanging a 40-inch TV on it is unmet — use a rated commercial TV wall mount.

lines.key: #8 (4 mm) countersunk wood screw, cleat strip
lines.label: #8 (4 mm) countersunk wood screw, cleat strip
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 4 FRENCH CLEATS: screw each cleat strip to the wall with its bevel on top, sloping down toward the wall, into a stud or a fixing rated for the load, then hang the cell so its hook drops in behind the bevel.
The list gives one printed strip per cleat. For a long run, rip a timber batten to the strip's bevel and hang several cells from it instead.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
